title: Adequate-moduli algebra adjunction has universally power-lifting nil kernel
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $R$ a commutative $k$-algebra, and $\phi:\mathcal X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ an adequate moduli space [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $C$ be any commutative $R$-algebra. Write $\mathcal C=\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}\otimes_R C$ for the quasi-coherent commutative algebra obtained by tensor pullback: on an affine scheme object $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\to\mathcal X$ it is the algebra associated to $A\otimes_R C$. Quasi-coherent algebras and their global sections use [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra], and tensor extension uses [def-weil-module-base-change]. Put $D=\Gamma(\mathcal X,\mathcal C)$ and let $u:C\to D$ send $c$ to the compatible family of sections $1\otimes c$. For every commutative $C$-algebra $C'$, form $u_{C'}:C'\to C'\otimes_C D$, $c'\mapsto c'\otimes1$. Every element of $\ker u_{C'}$ is nilpotent, and for every $d'\in C'\otimes_C D$ there are an integer $N>0$ and $c'\in C'$ with $u_{C'}(c')=(d')^N$. There are no finite-generation, flatness, Noetherian or absolute diagonal-separation hypotheses.

source.place: Alper, published version, Lemma 5.2.6, printed p.508, together with Proposition 3.3.5, Definition 3.3.1 and Remark 3.3.2, printed pp.497--498. Tensor form of the algebra adjunction unit. Primary PDF read online at https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: By the adequate-moduli definition, $R\simeq\Gamma(\mathcal X,\mathcal O)$ and every surjection of quasi-coherent algebras on $\mathcal X$ lifts positive powers on global sections (take the identity etale test of $\operatorname{Spec}R$). The affine-target criterion therefore makes $\phi$ adequately affine. Choose $P=R[T_c:c\in C]$ with evaluation $T_c\mapsto c$ and $I=\ker(P\to C)$; evaluation is surjective because every $c$ is the image of $T_c$, so $P/I\simeq C$.

source.place: Alper Lemma 5.2.6, printed p.508, using Lemma 5.2.1, printed p.507; online published PDF read, local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal Z=\mathcal X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}P$, with projection $f:\mathcal Z\to\operatorname{Spec}P$. Adequate affineness persists by the affine-target base-change lemma. The polynomial projection $\operatorname{Spec}P\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is flat, hence $R\to P$ is flat by the affine flatness criterion. Apply flat scalar-sections to $\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$ and $R\to P$: its restriction is $\mathcal O_{\mathcal Z}$ by the structure-sheaf definition, so the canonical map $R\otimes_R P\to\Gamma(\mathcal Z,\mathcal O_{\mathcal Z})$ is an isomorphism. It identifies this ring with $P$ and sends $T_c$ to the structural section $1\otimes T_c$.

source.place: Alper Lemma 5.2.6, printed p.508, using Lemma 5.2.1, printed p.507; online published PDF read, local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Apply the ideal-quotient comparison to $f$, $\mathcal A=\mathcal O_{\mathcal Z}$ and $I\subseteq P$. Its source is $P/IP=P/I=C$. Its target is $D$: indeed the closed relative spectrum of $\mathcal O_{\mathcal Z}/I\mathcal O_{\mathcal Z}$ is $\mathcal X\times_R\operatorname{Spec}C=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_{\mathcal X}(\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}\otimes_RC)$. These identifications follow on affine tests from imposing the relations $I$ on $A\otimes_RP$, yielding $A\otimes_RC$, and from the relative-spectrum global-section identification. They send the class of each $T_c$ to $1\otimes c$, so the comparison map is exactly $u$. For any $C$-algebra $C'$, its tensor extension is consequently exactly $u_{C'}$, and the cited comparison gives both elementwise nilpotence of its kernel and the asserted positive-power lift. No tensor/global-section isomorphism for a nonflat extension is used.
